gap: No result ChatGPT got states named measurements of idle (standby) draw for the grid-charged backup units: The Solar Lab measured about 20 W for the BLUETTI Apex 300 (ESS News 19.5 W), about 58 W for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus and 80 W for the original Anker F3800. That works out to roughly 0.5, 1.4 and 1.9 kWh a day that a battery with no solar has to make up from the grid, or loses from its reserve during an outage.
standout_why: Compared against outagereadyhq.com (cited; it says outright 'We have not run these systems ourselves'; its only idle figure is an unsourced '20W idle draw' for the Apex 300 listed as a drawback, with nothing for the other units), solutionenergy.com/batteries/without-solar (maker specs, EnergySage price averages and FranklinWH's own 90% round-trip figure; no named test and no standby figures), and the franklinwh.com overview and datasheet (maker claims only). energysavvyhomes.com (cited) would not load because of a certificate error, so I could not check it. None of the pages I read set measured idle draw, measured usable Wh or measured inverter efficiency for the candidates side by side, with a tester and a date.
decides: Without solar, every kWh comes from the grid, and during an outage nothing tops the battery back up. That makes standby drain and usable energy count for more than the label capacity. On The Solar Lab's numbers the Apex 300 idles at about a third of the Jackery 5000 Plus and a quarter of the original F3800. That strengthens the case for the Apex 300, which Dealectric lists, for a 'charge and wait' backup. Against that, Outdoor Life got only 2,290 Wh (83%) out of the Apex 300's 2,765 Wh rating under a dehumidifier load. OutdoorGearLab got 3,790 Wh (93%) out of the DELTA Pro 3's 4,096 Wh. For hours of runtime per dollar, the DELTA Pro 3's measured energy is the stronger figure. No independent measurement exists for the Powerwall 3, FranklinWH aPower 2 or Enphase IQ 5P, so the installed systems can only be compared on maker specs.

findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'a single Apex 300 had an idle draw of right around 20W'.
